## Problem

The Reputation line in the score tooltip displays an awkward `×` symbol before the colon separator (e.g. `Reputation ×: 5`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Remove the `×` from the Reputation label in the score tooltip so it reads `Reputation: 5` instead of `Reputation ×: 5`.
2. All related documentation and i18n keys are updated consistently.
3. Full project test suite must pass with the change.

## Constraints

- The `×` symbol is used correctly elsewhere in the tooltip (e.g. showing multipliers like `×1.038`) — only remove it from the Reputation label.

## Existing state

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` line 95: `scoreBreakdownReputation: 'Reputation ×'`
- Line 303 builds the output: `${t(HUD_TOOLTIP_I18N_KEYS.scoreBreakdownReputation)}: ${repContribution}` → renders as `Reputation ×: 5`

## Desired change

- Change `'Reputation ×'` to `'Reputation'` on line 95 of `MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — Default English string templates

# Intake Brief — REFACTOR: break out core engine and individual games into their own projects. (CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17)

## Problem Statement

The Tableau Card Engine is a single flat monorepo where every example game is co-located with the shared engine code. This couples game development to the full repository, makes it hard to version or reuse the engine independently, and prevents building lean distributions that bundle only a selected subset of games.

## Users

- **Engine maintainer (primary)** — Maintains shared engine modules and the Gym demo suite; wants a standalone core-engine repo that can evolve, be versioned, and be pulled into any distribution without dragging all games along.
  - *Story:* As an engine maintainer I can work on `src/core-engine`, `src/card-system`, `src/rule-engine`, `src/ui`, `src/ai` and the Gym in one repo, so that engine changes do not require touching game repos.
- **Game developer** — Builds a single example game in isolation; wants to check out just that game plus the engine and run `npm run dev` / `npm test` / `npm run build` without cloning every other game.
  - *Story:* As a game developer I can clone `tce-golf` (or any game repo) which pulls the core engine as a submodule, so that I can iterate on that game with a fast, focused checkout (`tce-game = distribution with 1 game`).
- **Distribution builder / launcher maintainer** — Assembles and ships a playable bundle (web + desktop binary) that contains the core engine plus a chosen set of 1..n games.
  - *Story:* As a distribution builder I can configure which game submodules are checked out in the launcher repo and run `npm run build` / `npm run package` to produce a web build and an Electron binary that show only the included games in the Game Selector.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Core-engine repo defined and extractable** — A standalone core-engine repository exists (or a concrete extraction plan + script is delivered) containing everything shared across games: `src/core-engine`, `src/card-system`, `src/rule-engine`, `src/ui`, `src/ai`, `src/balance-cards` (if shared), the Gym (`example-games/gym`), the launcher shell (`src/ui/GameSelectorScene`, `src/ui/createCardGame`), Electron launcher (`electron/`), shared assets under `public/assets`, and shared configs (`tsconfig.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `package.json` engine dependencies). Git history for moved files is preserved where feasible.
2. **Per-game repos with reverse submodule** — Each example game (golf, beleaguered-castle, blackjack, sushi-go, feudalism, lost-cities, main-street, coloretto) has its own GitHub repo with a consistent layout that pulls the core engine as a git submodule for standalone development; `npm install`, `npm run dev`, `npm run build`, and `npm test -- --project unit` (or equivalent targeted run) succeed in a `game + engine` checkout and path aliases (`@core-engine/*`, `@card-system/*`, `@rule-engine/*`, `@ui/*`, `@ai/*`) resolve correctly across the submodule boundary. Documented exception: games may vendor only their own `example-games/<game>/` tree.
3. **Launcher distribution assembles N games via submodules** — The main Tableau-Card-Engine repo acts as the launcher/distribution repo: it bundles the core engine plus a configurable set of games checked out as git submodules (e.g. under `games/` or `example-games/`), the Game Selector enumerates only the checked-out games, and `npm run build` (web, `dist/` with `/Tableau-Card-Engine/` base) and `npm run build:electron` / `npm run package` (desktop binary via Electron) succeed for any selection of 1..n games including the boundary cases of 1 game and all games.
4. **Dev workflows and Gym preserved** — `npm run dev` (HMR on port 3000), `vite`/`tsconfig` alias resolution, and the Gym demo scenes all continue to work from the core-engine repo and from the launcher distribution; Gym remains the canonical core-engine feature demonstrator and does not move to a game repo.
5. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** — `npm run build` succeeds and the relevant test profile passes in the launcher distribution with its default game set (full suite on release; unit + build at minimum before any push per AGENTS.md quality gates).

## Constraints

- Integration mechanism is **git submodules** (option a) — not npm packages or npm workspaces. No npm publication of the engine in this phase.
- **No CI required** in this phase — neither the core-engine repo nor the per-game repos need new GitHub Actions pipelines; existing `pr-checks.yml` / `package.yml` / `deploy.yml` remain on the launcher repo as-is.
- The launcher repo remains the deployable web + Electron distribution; game repos do not deploy independently.
- Preserve permissive-license posture (MIT / CC0) and existing toolchain (Phaser 4 RC, TypeScript strict, Vite, Vitest, Electron).
- Avoid breaking existing developer workflows more than necessary; submodule setup must be documented with copy-paste commands (`git clone --recurse-submodules`, `git submodule update --init --recursive`).
- Keep changes surgical — do not speculatively introduce versioning, changelogs, or release automation beyond what is needed to make the submodule composition build.

## Existing State

- Flat monorepo with a single `package.json` (v0.1.15), single `vite.config.ts` (path aliases for `@core-engine`, `@card-system`, `@rule-engine`, `@ui`, `@ai`), single `tsconfig.json`, and single `index.html` / `main.ts` unified entry point that hard-imports every game scene and registers them in `GAMES` for `GameSelectorScene`.
- Shared engine code under `src/` (`core-engine`, `card-system`, `rule-engine`, `ui`, `ai`, `balance-cards`); example games under `example-games/` (gym, golf, beleaguered-castle, blackjack, sushi-go, feudalism, lost-cities, main-street, coloretto); Gym is the interactive demo suite for core-engine features.
- Electron launcher under `electron/` with `build:electron` / `start:electron` / `package` scripts; `.gitmodules` does not exist; production build targets GitHub Pages at `/Tableau-Card-Engine/` and desktop binaries via `electron-builder`.
- Tests under `tests/` with Vitest projects (unit, browser, smoke, dev, tutorial E2E); game scenes and core modules are tightly coupled via static imports in `main.ts`.

## Desired Change

- Extract a **core-engine repository** that owns all shared code plus Gym and the launcher shell (GameSelector, Electron host). The extraction should be reproducible and preserve history (e.g. via `git filter-repo` / `git subtree` or a documented manual move — exact tooling is an implementation detail but must be recorded).
- Move each **example game to its own GitHub repo** (one repo per game, consistent layout). Each game repo composes a runnable project by pulling the core engine as a git submodule — i.e. a game checkout is itself a minimal TCE distribution with 1 game. Submodule pointer + local Vite/TS configs make engine imports resolve without publishing a package.
- Retain the **main Tableau-Card-Engine repo as the launcher/distribution repo** that composes the core engine with any subset of game submodules. Provide a simple mechanism (submodule presence, config file, or CLI flag) to specify which games are included in a given build, so `npm run build` and `npm run package` produce a distribution containing exactly 1..n games (web + binary). The Game Selector must discover games dynamically from the checked-out set rather than hardcoding all imports.
- Update docs (`README.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `public/assets/CREDITS.md` where relevant) and add submodule setup / distribution-build instructions. No new CI or npm publishing is required in this phase.

## Key Files

- `package.json` — Split / slim per-repo manifests; launcher and game repos need correct deps and scripts (`dev`, `build`, `build:electron`, `package`, `test`).
- `vite.config.ts` — Alias resolution must work across submodule boundaries; launcher needs dynamic game discovery instead of static imports.
- `tsconfig.json` — Path aliases and `include` paths must cover submodule layouts.
- `main.ts` — Unified entry point / GameSelector registration; must become dynamic (enumerate checked-out games rather than hardcoding all scenes).
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` — Game catalogue / registry (`REGISTRY_KEY_GAMES`); needs to handle a variable game set.
- `src/core-engine/**`, `src/card-system/**`, `src/rule-engine/**`, `src/ui/**`, `src/ai/**`, `src/balance-cards/**` — Shared engine code that stays in core.
- `example-games/gym/**` — Stays in core as the engine feature demonstrator.
- `example-games/<game>/**` — Each moves to its own repo (golf, beleaguered-castle, blackjack, sushi-go, feudalism, lost-cities, main-street, coloretto).
- `electron/**` — Launcher host; stays in core/launcher, must build against the composed distribution.
- `public/assets/**` — Shared card/back assets stay in core; game-specific assets move with their game or are documented as shared vs. game-owned.
- `index.html` — Entry HTML; must work in both core-only and composed builds.
- `.gitmodules` (new) — Submodule declarations for launcher→games and game→core compositions.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md` — Require updates for new repo layout, submodule workflows, and distribution builds.
- `scripts/**` — Build/test helpers (e.g. `run-ci-tests.sh`, `vite-transcript-plugin.ts`, `build-electron-main.mjs`) may need path adjustments.

## Related Work

- **Potentially related work items:**
  - `Scaffold Card Game Engine project (CG-0MLSFU7300TLFCBH)` — completed — established the current flat-monorepo structure, toolchain, and path aliases that this refactor will decompose.
  - `Create a Gym (CG-0MP3XQBL4008QK8S)` — completed — Gym is the canonical core-engine demonstrator that must remain in the core repo per producer direction.
- **Potentially related docs (paths):**
  - `README.md` — repo layout, quick-start, deployment model.
  - `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — project structure, path aliases, adding a game, building/packaging.
  - `AGENTS.md` — monorepo layout, SLL requirement, quality gates, worklog rules; needs updating for the new multi-repo model.
  - `vite.config.ts` / `tsconfig.json` — alias and build configuration that must span submodules.
  - `main.ts` / `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` — current static game registration that must become dynamic.
  - `electron/launcher-config.ts` / `electron/content-locator.ts` — desktop content resolution for the launcher.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Submodule ergonomics** — Git submodules are notoriously easy to misuse (detached HEAD, forgotten `--recurse-submodules`). *Mitigation:* document exact clone/update commands, add a `scripts/setup.sh` or `npm run setup` helper if helpful, and keep the default launcher checkout including a known-good game set.
- **History preservation vs. effort** — Preserving full git history for moved files adds complexity (`filter-repo`/`subtree`). *Assumption:* history preservation is preferred but not blocking — a well-documented move with a single squashed history is acceptable if tooling proves too heavy; record the decision in the implementation plan.
- **Dynamic GameSelector discovery** — Replacing static imports with dynamic discovery (filesystem or manifest) may require Vite glob imports or a small codegen step. *Mitigation:* prototype the discovery mechanism early; keep a fallback static list for the initial cut.
- **Asset ownership ambiguity** — Some assets under `public/assets/` are shared vs. game-specific. *Mitigation:* audit `public/assets/CREDITS.md` and per-game asset usage; move only clearly game-owned assets with their game.
- **Scope creep** — Versioning, npm publishing, per-game CI, and release automation are natural follow-ons but are explicitly **out of scope** for this epic. *Mitigation:* file them as separate follow-up work items rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption:** No CI or npm publication is required in this phase (per producer). Web + binary builds from the launcher are sufficient validation.
- **Assumption:** Core engine contains "everything shared across games" — includes `balance-cards` and the launcher shell; Gym stays in core (per producer).

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "How should the core engine be consumed by individual game repos? (a) git submodule/subtrees, (b) npm package, or (c) monorepo workspaces?" — Answer (producer, this session): "(a) git submodule/subtrees." Source: interactive reply to intake interview Q1. Research: inspected `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `.gitmodules` (absent), `main.ts` static imports, `electron/` layout — confirmed current flat monorepo with no submodules or workspaces.
- Q: "What stays vs. what moves — which components belong in the standalone core-engine repo? Does Gym stay in core?" — Answer (producer, this session): "core engine contains everything that is shared across games, gym remains in the core." Source: interactive reply to intake interview Q2. Research: listed `src/` (`core-engine`, `card-system`, `rule-engine`, `ui`, `ai`, `balance-cards`), `example-games/` (8 games + gym), `public/assets/` — confirmed Gym is under `example-games/gym` and shared modules are under `src/`.
- Q: "How should builds and deployments change — CI, versioning, npm publication, per-game deploys, launcher assembly?" — Answer (producer, this session): "no CI, or npm publication yet but we do want to be able to build a web and binary distribution that includes a specified set of games, no CI in the games either, Yes main repo is a launcher." Source: interactive reply to intake interview Q3. Research: inspected `package.json` scripts (`build`, `build:electron`, `package`, `package:win/linux/mac`), `vite.config.ts` base handling for Pages vs. Electron, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` deployment section — confirmed current GitHub Pages + Electron packaging from the monorepo.

## Foundational Test-References

- `tests/gym/GymSceneSmoke.browser.test.ts` — Gym smoke coverage (must keep passing from core/launcher).
- `tests/smoke.phaser4.browser.test.ts` — Phaser 4 smoke.
- `tests/vite-config.test.ts` — Vite alias / build config coverage.
- `tests/electron/launch-smoke.test.ts` — Electron launcher smoke.
- Full suite (`npm test` / `npm run build`) — release gate for the launcher distribution with its default game set.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MTHTJLES009CRHQ** – Linter auto-fix: engine modules (completed)
- **CG-0MP2988UN009P9LM** – Extract shared HUD layer into core engine and adopt across games (completed)
- **CG-0MQN1BLHH0086LU8** – F2: ActiveEffect infrastructure in state & serialization (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: able, around, break, building, bundled (+23 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: able, break, building, card, core (+17 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: able, break, building, card, core (+17 more)

## Goal

Create the undo challenge completion warning dialog.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New method showUndoChallengeWarningDialog(challengeTitles: string[], onConfirm: () => void, onCancel: () => void) on MainStreetOverlayContent.
2. Dialog follows the established overlay pattern: backdrop depth 199, box depth 200, interactive elements depth 201, all children parented into hudContainer.
3. Dialog presents: title "Challenge Completion Undo", body text listing challenge titles being undone, "Keep Completed" (cancel undo) and "Undo Anyway" (proceed) buttons.
4. The "Keep Completed" option aborts the undo entirely — no state change, no log entry.
5. The "Undo Anyway" option proceeds with the undo and revokes the challenge completion.
6. i18n keys added following existing conventions (e.g. ms.undoChallengeConfirm, ms.undoChallengeKeep).
7. Reduced-motion respected (no animations).

## Key Files

- example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts — new showUndoChallengeWarningDialog method
- example-games/main-street/i18n/en.ts (and other locale files) — add dialog copy keys
- example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts — call dialog from performUndo

CG-0MU8MV43Z003LLOK (Core: per-action challenge evaluation in executeAction)
CG-0MU8MXZ0A007Z6Z0 (Core: per-action challenge evaluation for commands)

# Upgrades don't work from the hand (CG-0MUDA70FK003J8YL)

**Headline:** When an upgrade card is selected from the hand for targeting, all empty street slots are highlighted as selectable instead of only the businesses that match the upgrade's criteria. The correct behaviour (mirroring drag-drop buy-and-play) is to highlight only eligible businesses (green) and ineligible ones (red), with empty slots left unhighlighted.

## Problem statement

When an upgrade card is selected from the hand (entering the `placing-from-hand` targeting phase), all empty street slots are highlighted as selectable targets. But upgrades can only be applied to existing businesses that match the upgrade's `targetBusiness` and `requiredLevel` criteria — empty slots and non-matching businesses should not appear as valid targets.

## Users

- **Player** — Clicks an upgrade in hand to apply it to a business. Expects to see exactly which businesses can receive the upgrade highlighted on the street grid, and not to see empty slots or wrong businesses as options.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Empty slots are not highlighted during upgrade targeting:** When the pending hand card is an upgrade (`uiPhase === 'placing-from-hand'` and `hand[pendingHandIndex].family === 'upgrade'`), `drawEmptySlot` must not make empty slots selectable or highlight them with the `isSelectable` colour.
2. **Eligible businesses are highlighted:** When an upgrade is selected from hand, the street grid shows visual highlight overlays on businesses — green border for businesses matching the upgrade's `targetBusiness` and `requiredLevel` (and below `maxLevel`), red border for businesses that do not match.
3. **Ineligible business clicks produce feedback:** Clicking a non-matching business shows illegal-move feedback (shake + SFX + instruction text) and keeps the upgrade selected for retry.
4. **Highlights persist across `refreshAll()`:** The highlight overlays survive the `refreshAll()` / `refreshStreetGrid()` call that happens after selecting an upgrade.
5. **Highlights are cleared on exit:** Cancelling targeting (Escape, switching hand card, or applying) clears all highlight overlays and returns the scene to a clean state.
6. **All tests pass:** Existing `upgrade-hand-flow.browser.test.ts` tests continue to pass; new browser tests added for visual targeting highlights.
7. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- The fix must not affect business card placement (empty slots should still be highlighted during business card targeting).
- The highlight system should reuse the existing drag-drop highlight infrastructure (`dragHighlightRects` array, transparent border rectangles) to keep visual consistency.
- The highlight eligibility check mirrors `applyHandUpgradeToSlot`'s business-level criteria (`biz.name === card.targetBusiness`, `biz.level === card.requiredLevel`, `biz.level < biz.maxLevel`), without the affordability check (affordability errors are shown in the instruction text after the click).

## Existing state

- The hand-first click flow for upgrades was implemented in CG-0MT40EHB1005JP6D and shipped in v0.1.16.
- The drag-drop buy-and-play for upgrades was implemented in CG-0MT40FT21005GBK7 and ships the same.
- `MainStreetRendererDragDrop.showDragHighlights()` correctly skips empty slots for upgrades and highlights businesses as valid/invalid — but this is only used during drag-drop, not click-to-place targeting.
- `MainStreetRendererStreet.drawEmptySlot()` uses `isSelectable = s.uiPhase === 'placing-business' || s.uiPhase === 'placing-from-hand'`, which is true for both business and upgrade targeting, so it highlights ALL empty slots regardless of card type.
- `MainStreetTurnControllerPlaceSell.onSlotClick()` routes upgrade targeting correctly to `applyHandUpgradeToSlot()` — the click handling logic is correct; the issue is purely visual feedback (which slots/buses are highlighted before the click).

## Desired change

1. **Modify `drawEmptySlot`** (`MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`): Skip `isSelectable` rendering for empty slots when the pending hand card is an upgrade (check `scene.pendingHandIndex !== null && scene.state.hand?.[scene.pendingHandIndex]?.family === 'upgrade'`).
2. **Add `showTargetHighlights`** (`MainStreetRendererDragDrop.ts`): A lightweight function that creates highlight overlays for businesses matching a given upgrade card's eligibility (business-level check only, no affordability), using the existing `dragHighlightRects` infrastructure.
3. **Wire into `onHandUpgradeCardClick`** (`MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts`): After switching to `placing-from-hand` for an upgrade, call `showTargetHighlights` with the upgrade card id. **Caveat (wiring/persistence):** `onHandUpgradeCardClick` already calls `refreshAll()`, and `refreshAll()` -> `refreshStreetGrid()` calls `streetContainer.removeAll(true)`, destroying any rects added to the street container. Highlight creation must therefore run **after** the street rebuild; the recommended hook is the tail of `refreshStreetGrid()` (when `uiPhase === 'placing-from-hand'` and the pending hand card is an upgrade), which covers both the initial selection and subsequent refresh paths. Calling `showTargetHighlights` directly in `onHandUpgradeCardClick` is only safe if it runs after `refreshAll()`.
4. **Wire into `cancelPendingPlacement`** (`MainStreetTurnControllerPlaceSell.ts`): Clear highlights when cancelling targeting (defensive — the existing `refreshAll()` call already rebuilds the street container, but an explicit clear keeps the state clean and covers any future non-refresh exit path).
5. **Clear on click** (`onSlotClick`): The existing flow already calls `refreshAll()` which will clear stale highlights.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Highlight persistence through `refreshStreetGrid()`:** `streetContainer` is fully rebuilt during `refreshStreetGrid()`, so highlight rects added to it are destroyed. The fix must re-create highlights after each street rebuild (e.g. in `refreshStreetGrid` when `uiPhase === 'placing-from-hand'` and the pending card is an upgrade).
- **Business-level vs full eligibility:** The visual highlights check only business-level matching (`targetBusiness` + `requiredLevel` + `level < maxLevel`), not affordability or action budget. This is intentional — affordability errors are shown in the instruction text after the click.
- **Drag-drop regression:** Modifying `drawEmptySlot` and adding highlight functions must not affect the drag-drop flow. The drag-drop highlight system uses `showDragHighlights()` directly; the click-to-place system uses `showTargetHighlights()`.
- **Assumption:** The fix only needs to handle click-to-place targeting; market-click upgrade targeting (drag-drop) already works correctly via `showDragHighlights()`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** A natural extension is to also show highlights during market-click upgrade targeting, but that is out of scope.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — `drawEmptySlot` (modify `isSelectable` gating)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererDragDrop.ts` — new `showTargetHighlights` + `clearTargetHighlights` functions
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` — `onHandUpgradeCardClick` (wire in highlight call)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerPlaceSell.ts` — `cancelPendingPlacement` (clear highlights)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — export the new highlight function
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarketUtils.ts` — shared `isEligibleUpgradeTarget` eligibility predicate
- `example-games/main-street/README.md` — targeting-highlights documentation
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — docs-site UX/visual feedback entry
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-hand-flow.browser.test.ts` — add tests for visual targeting highlights

## Related work

- **CG-0MUAYBBOM006C9PK** "Upgrades cannot be played from the hand" (open, medium) — the original report; this item is a more specific follow-up about the visual targeting feedback bug.
- **CG-0MT40EHB1005JP6D** "Engine: implement hand-first click flow + target selection for upgrades" (completed, shipped v0.1.16) — implemented the click flow; missed the visual targeting highlight step.
- **CG-0MT40FT21005GBK7** "Engine: implement drag-drop buy-and-play for upgrades" (completed, shipped v0.1.16) — implemented drag-drop highlighting that works correctly; click-to-place should mirror it.
- **CG-0MT40CNO1002MSDC** "Browser tests: hand-first click flow for upgrades" (completed) — `tests/main-street/upgrade-hand-flow.browser.test.ts`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions asked — the bug description and code analysis provided sufficient detail to identify the root cause and a concrete fix.

### Plan review (2026-09-23)

Planning was auto-skipped (effort: Small, risk: Low) and the six review stages were run against the existing content:

1. **Requirements & AC alignment** — ACs 1-5 map to the stated problem and desired change; ACs 6-8 cover tests/docs/full-suite. No missing or contradictory ACs. Verified against the actual code paths (`drawEmptySlot`, `showDragHighlights`, `onHandUpgradeCardClick`, `cancelPendingPlacement`, `applyHandUpgradeToSlot`).
2. **Completeness** — description and ACs present; no children to check. All six predicted Key Files exist at the stated paths (the informal `## Key Files (predicted)` heading is not the machine-readable `**Key Files:**` section, so the format validator is a no-op). Corrected one factual inaccuracy in **Existing state** (`drawEmptySlot` also gates on `uiPhase === 'placing-business'`).
3. **Sequencing & dependencies** — no child items; the desired-change steps are internally ordered. No test-before-implementation child split needed at this size.
4. **Scope sizing** — single small bug fix, one deliverable increment; no decomposition needed.
5. **Acceptance & testability** — all ACs are pass/fail and testable via `tests/main-street/upgrade-hand-flow.browser.test.ts` plus new browser assertions on highlight overlays and empty-slot gating.
6. **Polish & handoff** — resolved an internal contradiction between "Desired change" step 3 and the "Highlight persistence" risk: because `refreshAll()` rebuilds `streetContainer`, highlights must be (re)created after the street rebuild (recommended hook: tail of `refreshStreetGrid()`). This is a clarification consistent with the Risks section, not an intent change.

AC coverage review (`run_coverage_review`): recommendation `proceed` (no children, no parent ACs to cover).

# Event-card select-then-act flow

## Goal

Make held event cards discardable by the player. Event cards currently auto-play on click, so they have no selectable state. Introduce a select-then-act flow (click selects; **[Play]** and **[Discard]** both offered) without regressing the one-click play path. Risk-driven decision point.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Clicking a held event card enters a selectable state and highlights it; the action bar offers **[Play]** and **[Discard]**.
- **[Play]** preserves today's `play-event` behaviour and action economy.
- The tutorial "Triggering Events" step (T23, `requiredAction: 'play-event'`) and its E2E parts pass unchanged; `tutorial-action-economy` tests pass.
- Go/no-go: if the selection change cannot preserve T23, the event UI is deferred to a follow-up work item and the existing one-click play path is left untouched — the decision and rationale are recorded on this item. The engine penalty (F1) still covers event cards either way.
- Parent AC traceability — **UI affordance and trigger:** Once a hand card is selected, a **[Discard]** button is rendered in the action bar's rightmost slot — the position occupied by **[End Turn]** in the market phase (the same slot `placing-from-hand` currently gives **[Cancel]**). Clicking it discards the selected hand card and returns the UI to the market phase; **[Cancel]** remains available alongside it (shifted left). No confirmation dialog is shown (producer decision). The button is created via `createActionButton`, positioned via the existing SLL layout values, and labelled with the reputation cost it will deduct.

## Minimal Implementation

- Change the event hand-card click in `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` to select (enter a selectable phase) instead of calling `onPlayHeldEvent` directly.
- Add a **[Play]** button to the selectable phase in `MainStreetRendererHud.ts` that calls the existing `onPlayHeldEvent`.
- Guard the tutorial gate, verify T23, and revert + file the follow-up if it regresses.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the Discard button and handler item.

## Key Files

## Failure Signature

- Test name: `<suite exited 1>: npm --silent test` (full-suite run — the non-zero exit is not a named failing test)
- Failing commit: 1eb6d6448dfe0b62ffd2c7fafbdb2fb1ae52e130
- CI job: (not available)

## Failure Classification

The unit stage passed **every** file — `Test Files 396 passed (396)`,
`Tests 6883 passed | 8 skipped (6891)` — and the run exited 1 solely because of
Vitest's transient worker RPC timeout at teardown:

```
Error: [vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "onTaskUpdate"
```

This is the **known CPU-contention teardown flake**, not a genuine assertion
failure. Two mitigations are already in place:

1. `maxWorkers: 4` for the `unit` project in `vite.config.ts`
   (CG-0MS9M5UJP005PWD3).
2. Retry-once on the transient signatures in
   `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`, wired into the unit and browser stages of
   `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` (CG-0MS9M5UJP005PWD3, CG-0MSCI73RH004VPCE).

**Why this still needs work (evidence analysis):** the poisoned unit stage began
at `05:09:28` (BST) and lasted `117.36s`, while this work item was created at
`04:11:31Z` (= `05:11:31` BST) — consistent with the poisoned 117s attempt being
either the *only* attempt (retry not triggered) or the *retry* itself (both
attempts poisoned). Either way the suite exited 1 with all tests green, so the
current mitigation is not sufficient at this contention level. **Establishing
which of those two it was is the discriminator for the fix.**

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```

```

## Steps To Reproduce

2. Run the full suite: `npm --silent test` (Vitest + `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`; there is no pytest suite in this repository)
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item — in particular the `[retry]` line emitted by `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`, which establishes whether a retry was attempted and whether it recovered

## Impact

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The full suite (`npm --silent test`) exits 0 when run against the latest `dev`, with no unhandled `[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "onTaskUpdate"` error.

# Context-budget pre-push gate blocks all dev pushes (AGENTS.md 46024 B > 45898 B)

Discovered while pushing CG-0MUDA70FK003J8YL (docs-only commit 3d9d1ba7) — `discovered-from:CG-0MUDA70FK003J8YL`.

## Symptom

Every `git push` from the main checkout (or any worktree based on current `dev`) fails with:

```
ERROR: Context budget exceeded committed thresholds.
  project_agents (46024 B > 45898 B), total (46024 B > 45898 B)
```

## Root cause

`AGENTS.md` grew to **46024 B** in commit `2283a146` (CG-0MUF0LU4X006IXXU, "accept all-passed transient retry + emit runner summary"), while `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` still allows **45898 B**. The pre-push context-budget gate (F6, SA-0MSLK7XNZ00366YY) therefore blocks **all** pushes to `dev`. This is the same class of drift as CG-0MTCRF0K2006N0HR (41706 B > 41692 B).

The current work item (CG-0MUDA70FK003J8YL) changes no context-surface files (`AGENTS.md` untouched; only `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`), so the sanctioned `CONTEXT_BUDGET_SKIP=1` bypass was used for its push, per the documented precedent.

## Fix

Refresh the committed thresholds to match the current startup context surface (chore/infra):

```bash
python3 ~/.pi/agent/skills/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py \
  --repo-root . --include-hidden \
  --thresholds docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json --generate-thresholds
```

or hand-edit `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` to `project_agents = 46024`, `total = 46024`.

## Verify

```bash
python3 ~/.pi/agent/skills/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py \
  --repo-root . --include-hidden \
  --thresholds docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json
```

must report no budget exceeded, after which ordinary pushes to `dev` succeed without `CONTEXT_BUDGET_SKIP`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` reflects the current `AGENTS.md` size.
2. `measure_context.py` reports no threshold exceeded at `dev` HEAD.
3. A subsequent push to `dev` succeeds without `CONTEXT_BUDGET_SKIP=1`.
